summary: Intermittent GPU starvation in dedicated pool triggered by background snapshotter I/O spiral
description: Issue summary: Customer experiencing repeated p99/p50 throughput regression on dedicated capacity during midday windows. Symptoms correlated with GPU allocation failures and sustained queueing even after autoscaler added capacity. Initial customer report described spikes in 'request queued' and streams timing out.
impact: Multiple production endpoints for Neptune Analytics' dedicated pool saw up to 60% drop in sustained throughput for 30-90 minute windows; some live inference streams hit timeouts and 429s. Business impact: degraded user experience on customer-facing features and elevated support tickets.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run steady small-stream traffic to dedicated pool (Neptune prod config) with mixed short/long requests. 2) Trigger background snapshot backup job that writes incremental checkpoints to the same NVMe-backed nodes. 3) Observe autoscaler add events and repeated GPU attachment failures with queued requests growing.
logs_summary: Scheduler logs show increased attach/release churn at 2026-03-10T14:12:xxZ. Kernel i/o wait elevated on nodes host-wn-12 and host-wn-14. Serving runtime reported 'gpu_attach_timeout' and 'batcher_wait_exceeded' between 14:12-15:40Z. NVMe SMART metrics indicate 35-40% increased write latency during the window. Grafana panels: /d/cluster/dedicated-pool?from=... (link shared in comments).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy background writer (snapshotter) was saturating host storage I/O which increased NVMe latency -> GPU driver attach latencies -> batcher stalls -> autoscaler misinterprets latency as capacity shortage and continues to scale, leading to eviction/attach storms.

comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reports intermittent high queue length and p99 spikes starting around midday. Attached customer metrics and sample request IDs.
SRE (Liam): Found NVMe write latency spike on two nodes correlated with times of degraded throughput; collecting dstat and iostat traces.
Customer (Neptune SE): We kicked off routine checkpoint backups at 14:00 UTC; paused after Support asked. We see the drop after pause.
Eng (Maya Patel): Hypothesis: noisy snapshotter is blocking io scheduler, causing GPU device attach latencies. Proposing cgroup-based io limits and relocate snapshot jobs to utility pool.
SRE (Liam): Applied temporary mitigation by cancelling the in-progress snapshot job for Neptune and pinning their serving tasks to other nodes; queueing returned to normal in ~6 minutes.
Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed degraded experience subsided after pause. Will keep ticket open until permanent mitigation is deployed.

Eng (Maya): Merged PR 2184 to enforce snapshotter io.rate limits and added scheduler predicate to avoid colocating heavy IO writers with active inference tenants. Patch scheduled to rollout to prod 2026-03-12.
SRE (Liam): Rolled changes to us-west on 2026-03-12 18:30; monitoring shows no recurrence in 48 hours. Marking resolved pending customer sign-off.
Customer (Neptune SE): Confirmed normal throughput on their end and closed their active incident. Thank you team.
resolution: Root cause: snapshotter-induced host storage I/O saturation causing elevated NVMe write latencies, which in turn increased GPU attach and kernel IO wait times. This produced batcher stalls that the autoscaler misinterpreted as capacity shortage, triggering attach/evict churn and sustained throughput drop. Fix: applied immediate customer-side snapshot pause (mitigation) and deployed permanent changes: 1) rate limiting for snapshotter I/O via cgroups, 2) scheduler affinity rule to separate checkpoint writers from inference hosts, 3) autoscaler heuristic adjustment to ignore transient attach latency spikes (increased stabilization window and added attach-failure dampening).
follow_up_actions: Add automated detection alert for sustained host IO latency correlated with attach failures
